# dsh-win-bash
English | 中文
Git Bash command execution for DeepSeek Harness on Windows.
## What it does

The shipped DSH composition gates its two shell stacks by platform. On Windows
the host composes `@d

eepseek-ai/dsh-pwsh-sandbox` (PowerShell) and every agent
preset mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh`

; the bash stack stays disabled
because `dsh-bash-local` spawns a bare `bash` resolved through `PATH

` — which
on Windows is `C:\Windows\system32\bash.exe`, the **WSL launcher**, not Git
Bash. A WSL sh

ell has a different filesystem view and no `C:\`-style paths, so
it is not a drop-in Windows shell.
This plugin adds the missing piece:

- a `ctx.shell` provider that spawns an **explicitly resolved Git Bash**
executable (`<git>\bin\bash

.exe -c <command>`), inheriting every upstream
mechanic: managed process groups, timeout/abort class

ification, bounded
output with spill files, the model-friendly environment (`NO_COLOR`,
`TERM=dumb`,

`PAGER=cat`), background jobs, and the file sandbox;
- the shipped model-facing **`bash` tool** wir
ed to that executor.

It composes **beside** the pwsh stack rather than replacing it: the loader row
declares `isolate: {

shell: 'win-bash' }`, which puts the executor and the tool
into a private service realm. The host's

`ctx.shell` (pwsh) is neither
replaced nor duplicated, so the preset's `pwsh` tool keeps working unt

ell` (pwsh) is neither
replaced nor duplicated, so the preset's `pwsh` tool keeps working untouched.

Either form writes the profile dependency and appends `dsh-win-bash` to
`dsh.profile.bundles`; the p

lugin's own `cordis.patch.yml` supplies the loader
row. The host picks the new bundle up on the next

start (the profile
reconciliation hot-reloads the row when the app is running).
To use it in another profile, repeat the command with that profile name.
## Configuration

All knobs live on the `win-bash` row (override from the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` with a bare `-

id: win-bash / config: {...}` entry — a
patch replaces the row's whole `config`):
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `bashPath` | `''` | Absolute path to `bash.exe`. Empty = auto-detect. |
| `promptHint` | `true` |

Add a one-line system-prompt section preferring `bash` over `pwsh`. |
| `sandboxFallback` | `auto` |

What a proven confined-spawn failure means on this host — see below. |
| `timeoutMs` | `120000` | D

efault foreground timeout (upstream default). |
| `maxTimeoutMs` | `600000` | Cap for per-call timeo

ut overrides. |
| `maxOutputBytes` | `64000` | Per-stream in-memory cap; overflow spills to disk. |

| `maxSpillBytes` | `67108864` | Per-stream full-output spill cap. |
| `graceMs` | `3000` | Kill esc

alation and post-exit pipe-drain grace. |
| `cwd` | *(unset)* | Default working directory; the sessi
on workspace wins per call. |
### Confined Git Bash cannot initialize today (`sandboxFallback`)

On Windows, the upstream ACL runner (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`)
spawns confined childre

n under a `WRITE_RESTRICTED` token, and **Git Bash
cannot initialize under it**. Two routes to the s

ame death —
`STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED`, exit `0xC0000142`, reported by the tool as
`(no output) [exit
code: 3221225794]` — are known:

1. **Console-less host.** The runner spawns console children that inherit the
host console (its own

docs: "Console isolation is unavailable"; the
`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`/`CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE` variants die u

nder the restricted
token). A DSH **desktop** app launched from Explorer/Start menu is a GUI
process

with no console anywhere in its tree, so console children die at
DLL init. Reported from a real des

ktop install, where the shipped `pwsh`
tool died the same silent way.
2. **msys shared object (every

host).** The msys runtime behind Git Bash
creates `\BaseNamedObjects\msys-*` during init; the restr

icted token denies
it (`0xC0000022`) and bash dies with a fatal-error stack trace on stderr.
Reprodu

ced with the real shipped runner on a dev machine: `cmd.exe` and
`powershell.exe` survive the identi

cal spawn (console or not) — only bash
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- **Windows only.** The row is gated `process.platform !== 'win32'`; on POSIX
the shipped bash stack

already runs and a second `bash` tool would collide.
- **`pwsh` remains available.** Removing it wo

uld mean restating an agent
preset's whole plugin list, which silently drifts on every DSH upgrade (

a
renamed package there fails the preset mount for every session). The
`promptHint` section steers t

he model to `bash` instead; sessions that
should never see pwsh can use a preset without it.
- **Git

Bash path semantics are MSYS semantics.** `/f/...` paths, and Windows
paths with backslashes may ne

ed quoting — ordinary Git Bash behavior, the
same model-facing surface as any Git Bash user.
- **The

confined sandbox path is inherited, not re-implemented.** In
`workspace-write`/`read-only` modes th

e upstream windows-acl runner wraps
our argv; only the wrapped executable changes.
- **No Windows ho

st can sandbox Git Bash today.** Two independent routes kill
the confined child before the command r

uns: a console-less GUI host (the
runner's own documented limitation — launching DSH from a terminal

avoids
only this one), and the msys runtime's denied `\BaseNamedObjects\msys-*`
object under the re

stricted token, which hits every host regardless of how
DSH was launched. Both are upstream limitati

ons of the ACL runner, not
something the plugin can fix by choosing a different shell — `pwsh` dies

the same way on the first route. Under `sandboxFallback: auto` the plugin
answers such a call with a

denial and lets the user authorize a wider mode.
- **Confined Git Bash is broken on every Windows h

ost, not just desktops.**
Under the runner's restricted token the msys runtime cannot create its
`\B

aseNamedObjects\msys-*` shared object (`0xC0000022` → bash dies
`0xC0000142`); reproduced with the r

eal shipped runner, where cmd and pwsh
survive the identical spawn. `sandboxFallback` is therefore t

he working
configuration for Windows — under `auto` it routes every such call through
user authoriza
tion instead of quietly running unconfined.
